tagline: It seemed way colder back then
journal:
I can't remember the last time we had a real cold winter, the last one was probably when my daughter was about six years old, we'd had two blizzards roll in back to back, then an extended freeze. It was quite rare for them to cancel school back then, we lived in the north so you'd always expect a little bit of snow but this was enough to bring everything to a halt for a week or so.

When the school rang me in the morning I remember being so stressed out, I'd not got anyone to look after her while I was at work, I was ringing around parents and relatives trying to find anyone who might brave the journey to our house and do some childcare until I got home. Then right as I was about to give up, my own phone rang out. Apparently the boiler in the office had broken down when the staff came to open up in the morning and they'd called to let everyone know they weren't required to come into work that day.

Thanks to that old broken down boiler, we got to spend the whole day making memories in the snow.
prompt: Low behind them in deep snow, on a short pasture, the pale winter sun ahead catches the side of the father's face as he looks down at his daughter, her mittened hand lifted to hold his as they walk away.

music.why: A father looking back fondly on a rare snow day spent walking hand in hand with his young daughter under a pale winter sun calls for warm, nostalgic, gentle arrangements.
